report.source_text: CT of the facial region with contrast showed abnormal soft tissue thickening in the region of the right side of the face with thickening and enhancement of right lacrimal gland, mild pre-septal swelling, thickening and enhancement of temporalis, lateral pterygoid and muscles of mastication on the right side. These findings were likely representing infected/inflammatory process (figure 2). There was pansinusitis with air fluid levels in bilateral maxillary sinuses and sphenoid sinuses. Pneumatised petrous temporal bone apex was visualised with fluid within it. There were ill-defined hypodensities in bilateral cerebellar hemispheres and right temporal lobe. These findings indicated possibility of an infarction.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old male with diabetes, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and recent COVID-19 presented with a black lesion on his right cheek, right eye swelling, ophthalmoplegia, and black eschar on the right cheek and hard palate. CT imaging revealed extensive soft tissue thickening, pansinusitis, and possible cerebral infarction. Histopathology of biopsy specimens confirmed numerous aseptate fungal hyphae in the right cheek skin, right eyeball, and nasal tissue. Microbiology culture identified Rhizopus spp. Emergency surgical intervention included right face debridement, right eye exenteration, and bilateral functional endoscopic sinus surgery. Postoperative CT confirmed surgical changes and maturation of infarcts.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with black lesion on right cheek, right eye swelling, right eye ophthalmoplegia, and black eschar on the right cheek and hard palate, with risk factors including DM, HTN, IHD, and recent COVID-19.

CT scan showed abnormal soft tissue thickening, thickening and enhancement of right lacrimal gland and mastication muscles, pansinusitis with air fluid levels, and possible infarction in cerebellar hemispheres and right temporal lobe.
Histopathology confirmed numerous aseptate fungal hyphae in biopsy specimens from right cheek skin, right eyeball, and nasal tissue.
Microbiology culture from nasal and throat smear revealed broad coenocytic (A-septate) hyphae and culture-grown Rhizopus spp.
Emergency right face debridement, right eye exenteration, and bilateral functional endoscopic sinus surgery were performed.
Postoperative head CT showed interval removal of right orbital structures and right cheek soft tissue, and maturation of infarcts.
